policies.title: Current bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemptions
policies.summary: China MFA's current mutual-agreement register expressly records ordinary-passport coverage for these foreign passports; the register is the current source for each agreement's entry-into-force date.
conditions: The current MFA register records these remaining ordinary-passport agreement effective dates: MV 2022-05-20; MU 2013-10-31; QA 2018-12-21; WS 2025-04-02; SM 1985-07-22; RS 2017-01-15; SC 2013-06-26; SG 2024-02-09; SB 2024-12-28; SR 2014-05-06; TH 2024-03-01; TO 2016-08-19; AE 2018-01-16; UZ 2025-06-01.
The register says specified valid passports are permitted stays of less than 30 days; a longer stay requires residence formalities under local rules.

This ordinary-passport visitor normalization does not establish work, study, residence, transit-only, tour-group, port-visa, diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs, special-document, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Forty-eight unilateral ordinary-passport visa waivers through 2026
policies.summary: The current NIA list and MFA FAQ establish a 30-day unilateral ordinary-passport waiver for these 48 nationalities, effective only through 31 December 2026.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The FAQ says the waiver applies at sea, road and air ports open to foreign nationals unless law, regulation or a bilateral arrangement provides otherwise.
Work, study, news coverage and similar purposes require a visa in advance; border authorities still examine purpose and admissibility.
It does not establish residence, special-document, diplomatic/official, Hainan/regional, port-visa, or transit-only treatment.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: unilateral visa waiver without stated expiry
policies.summary: China MFA's current FAQ places Brunei in the current unilateral 30-day ordinary-passport waiver and states no expiry date.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The current FAQ states no expiry date; it does not make the waiver permanent by treaty or remove the authority to amend it.
Work, study, news coverage, residence, special documents, diplomatic/official travel, regional programmes, port visas, security and individual admissibility remain separate.

policies.title: Russia ordinary passports: unilateral visa waiver through 2027
policies.summary: China MFA's current FAQ places Russia in the current unilateral 30-day ordinary-passport waiver through 31 December 2027.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The FAQ confirms the unilateral waiver applies to individuals as well as tour groups; this policy does not normalize the separate bilateral authorized-tour-group arrangement.
Work, study, news coverage, residence, special documents, diplomatic/official travel, regional programmes, port visas, security and individual admissibility remain separate.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance visa required baseline
policies.summary: The Exit and Entry Administration Law requires foreigners to apply to visa authorities abroad unless a legal exception applies. The current unilateral and mutual official schedules establish the covered ordinary-passport exceptions above; this policy records the nationwide short-visitor baseline for all remaining foreign catalog passports except special PRC/HK/Macao/Taiwan cases retained as unresolved.
conditions: Apply to the Chinese visa-issuing authority abroad for the ordinary visa appropriate to the actual visitor purpose; authorities can require application information, an interview and, where required, a written invitation.

This is the nationwide ordinary-passport baseline only. It excludes residence-permit holders, 24-hour and State Council transit arrangements, regional/Hainan programmes, authorized tour groups, port visas, crew, diplomatic/official/service/public-affairs/special documents, and emergency or other narrow statutory routes.

A visa can be refused for statutory security, public-order, health, fraud, financial-guarantee, documentation and other listed grounds; entry remains subject to border inspection and individual admissibility.

conflicts.explanation: The current MFA agreement register covers Dominica only for a public-affairs-marked ordinary passport, not the catalog's ordinary passport; the statutory advance-visa baseline applies.
The current MFA register expressly records Samoa ordinary-passport mutual visa exemption effective 2 April 2025.

unresolved.reason: The reviewed law protects Chinese citizens' legitimate exit-and-entry rights, but the reviewed material does not directly establish a right-of-return normalization for the catalog's ordinary-passport pair. No citizenship status is inferred.

The reviewed foreigner-visa law and ordinary-passport schedules do not directly map a Hong Kong passport to mainland entry. Home-return permit, Chinese-nationality and residence/document conditions are outside this ordinary foreign-passport normalization.

The reviewed foreigner-visa law and ordinary-passport schedules do not directly map a Macao passport to mainland entry. Home-return permit, Chinese-nationality and residence/document conditions are outside this ordinary foreign-passport normalization.

The reviewed foreigner-visa law and ordinary-passport schedules do not directly map a Taiwan passport to mainland entry. Taiwan Compatriot Permit and related identity/document conditions are outside this ordinary foreign-passport normalization.
